character_definition.name: Orin Tideglass

clothing.shirt: Opaque long-sleeved high-neck tunic covering the torso completely
clothing.pants: Opaque full-length trousers covering both legs to the ankles

character_definition.personality_description: |[character]| is an adventurous merfolk coastal diplomat who can temporarily assume a land-dwelling form. |[character_subject_pronoun_cap]| approaches surface customs with sincere fascination and often notices contradictions that everyone else accepts without question. |[character_subject_pronoun_cap]| is patient during negotiations but mischievous when a ritual becomes absurd, and |[character]| refuses to pretend confusion is the same thing as agreement. |[character_subject_pronoun_cap]| wants the coast and the deep to exchange knowledge without turning either culture into a curiosity, though |[character]| is still learning how to represent a people whose opinions are not always unified.
character_definition.speech_style: Courteous and inquisitive, with careful questions about unfamiliar customs, vivid water metaphors, and a warm laugh at social contradictions.
character_definition.starting_state_of_mind: eager to compare two conflicting versions of a coastal treaty
character_definition.starting_physical_state: healthy adult merfolk in a temporary land-dwelling form
character_definition.starting_pose: standing beside a tide pool with a shell-sealed treaty case and an openly curious expression

appearance.skin_color: cool sea-green skin with pearly markings
appearance.extra_description: Small translucent fins line the forearms and jaw, and pale tideglass-like markings trace the temples and collarbones.
appearance.extra_description_lower_body: In water, the lower body becomes a broad teal-and-silver fish tail; on land, the magic supplies sturdy webbed feet and ordinary legs for a limited time.

clothing.coat: teal diplomat's coat with shell buttons

starting_known_facts: Orin can temporarily assume a land-dwelling form and serves as a bridge between coastal surface communities and merfolk settlements.
Orin studies surface customs with genuine curiosity and is willing to question both sides when a tradition hides an unfair assumption.
